history.dynasty: Mewar (Rajputs; temple associated with King Gangdev of Garhbor; inscriptions date construction to 1444 AD, reign of Maharana Kumbha)
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: the famous Charbhuja temple is NOT in Nathdwara town - it stands at Garhbor village, Kumbhalgarh tehsil, Rajsamand district (~32 km from Kumbhalgarh, ~112 km from Udaipur). Documented with the corrected location. Charbhuja Nath is a four-armed form of Vishnu/Krishna; legend says the Pandavas worshipped the idol before their Himalayan journey, and King Gangdev recovered it from a river after a dream-command. The temple is famed for mirror work, gold inner shutters, silver outer shutters, and stone elephants at the entrance. Tradition says ~125 battles were fought defending the idol, which was submerged in water multiple times to protect it. Wikipedia coordinates 25.2667N 73.6833E vs geocoded street-level point - verify on site.

name: Charbhuja Temple
town: Garhbor (CSV town 'Nathdwara' is WRONG - Nathdwara is ~35 km away in the same district)
town_description: Garhbor is a historic village in Kumbhalgarh tehsil of Rajsamand district, set in the Aravalli hills on the Kumbhalgarh-Nathdwara road. Once the seat of the Bor Rajputs with its own fort, it is a pilgrimage halt between the Shrinathji temple town of Nathdwara and Kumbhalgarh Fort, surrounded by scrub forest and the seasonal Gomti river.

travel.railway: Falna railway station - about 70 km (verify); Kumbhalgarh road side is better reached via Nathdwara/Kankroli rail links (verify).
travel.road: On the Kumbhalgarh-Nathdwara road (SH-16/SH-12); about 32 km from Kumbhalgarh and 112 km from Udaipur by bus/taxi.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Jal Jhulni Ekadashi (August-September) for the big fair.
